name: Ladder Logic
title: Ladder Logic (IEC 61131-3:2013)

presenceList.meta: Ec4, Ec5, Ec7, Ec8, V4, D1, D3, S1

type.text: **The type is a PLC data type**: `BOOL`, `INT`, and `REAL` are checked by the vendor compiler
**There is no namespace**: A global tag shares one controller-wide space, and a POU's local variables are the only scope

construction.text: **The I/O image is global**: Every rung reads and writes the same process image
**A tag is writable from any rung**

memory.text: **There is no scope-exit release**: A resource is a coil or an instruction the scan resets
**There is no ownership model**: A tag is shared by every rung

error.text: **A fault bit is the failure path**: The program checks a bit, and no structure carries the failure

concurrency.text: **The scan is the only thread**: One pass reads the inputs, executes the rungs, and writes the outputs

platform.text: **A program runs on one controller family**: The vendor's runtime and I/O modules are the platform
**The standard is published**: IEC 61131-3 defines the languages and the program model, and the text is sold by the IEC
**Ordinary application work is out of reach**: There is no file, socket, or heap

performance.text: **A scan completes in a bounded time**: The cycle is deterministic

ecosystem.text: **The toolchain is proprietary**: A vendor sells the IDE and the runtime
**The IDE is locked to the vendor**: A project does not move between vendors unchanged
**A controller runs a program for decades**: The installed base keeps old firmware

**A compiled PLC library binds to a version**: Beckhoff ships libraries as *.compiled-library with a four-part version, increments the major digit when a new version is incompatible with the previous one, and fixes the version a project uses when the configuration activates on the target [@beckhoffLibDev; @beckhoffLibUse]

evolution.text: **The standard moves slowly**: The third edition is from 2013

domain.text: **The domain is industrial control**: A machine, a line, or a process
**The scan and the I/O image set the architecture**: A network of rungs over a fixed memory map

learning.text: **An electrician reads a rung**: The notation mirrors a relay circuit

syntax.text: **The notation is graphical and verbose**: A network of contacts and coils

testing.text: **The IDE simulates the controller**: A rung is forced and watched

security.text: **A tag has no access control inside the program**

reproducibility.text: **A project is downloaded to a controller**: The artifact is a vendor project file
**A dependency is a firmware version**: Nothing in the program pins it

interop.text: **There is no portable target**: A program runs on one controller family

tradeoffs: **The rung is the program**: A network of contacts and coils over one memory map
**The scan is the contract**: The cycle time bounds every response
**The vendor is the platform**: A project, a runtime, and an I/O module set come from one supplier
**The standard is shared, the implementations are not**: A program does not move between vendors
verdict: Ladder Logic is an industrial control language: the scan, the I/O image, and the rung notation make a machine's logic readable to an electrician, and the cycle is deterministic. What it charges is the global tag space, the fault-bit path, the single scan thread, the vendor runtime, and a standard that has not moved since 2013. Main strength: a notation the plant can read. Main weakness: the program is bound to one controller family.

energy.text: No independent energy or time benchmark for the language is recorded.

ai-readiness.text: Sparse public training data: models write it less reliably than a mainstream language [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

lifecycleNote: the third edition of the standard

delivery.note: Source builds inside the vendor toolchain

Beckhoff ships PLC libraries as *.compiled-library with a four-part version, increments the major digit when a new version is incompatible with the previous one, and fixes the library version a project uses when the configuration activates on the target
